nodes.name: Fault report in
nodes.notes: One door for every channel. WhatsApp, the care inbox and the driver app all POST here, so the pipeline below is written once instead of three times.

nodes.name: Store the report as it arrived

parameters.query:
insert into intake.report (channel, reporter, body, payload)
values ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb)
returning id

nodes.notes: Saved BEFORE the model sees it. If OpenAI is down, rate-limits us or returns nonsense, the complaint is already on disk - a lost complaint is a charger nobody fixes. Values are bound as $1..$4, never pasted into the SQL, because this text comes from the internet.

nodes.name: Read the complaint

attributes.name: site
attributes.description: The charging site, exactly as the reporter named it. Do not expand, correct or guess a fuller name.

attributes.name: charger_label
attributes.description: The charger as the reporter named it, for example 'charger 3' or 'the DC one'. Leave empty if they did not say which charger. Never invent one.

attributes.name: symptom
attributes.description: What is wrong, in at most eight words, using the reporter's own meaning.

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Exactly one of: critical, high, normal, low. critical = unsafe or smoke or sparks. high = the charger cannot deliver energy at all. normal = it works but something is wrong. low = cosmetic, or a question.

attributes.name: confident
attributes.description: True only if the complaint names the site and the symptom unambiguously. False if anything had to be guessed.

attributes.name: note
attributes.description: What is missing or ambiguous in this complaint, for the human who may have to read it. Empty if nothing is.

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You are reading a fault report written by a site host, a driver or a technician, in whatever mixture of languages they use. Extract only what the text actually says.

You are NOT diagnosing the fault and you are NOT resolving the charger to an identifier in any system. A reader of your output must be able to check every field against the sentence they sent.

If the text does not say which charger, leave charger_label empty and set confident to false. An empty field is a correct answer. An invented one sends a technician to the wrong site.

nodes.notes: Each field's description IS the prompt for that field. severity is restricted to four words here as a request - and again in the database as a constraint, because only one of those two can actually refuse.

nodes.name: gpt-5-nano
nodes.notes: Reasoning effort low, deliberately. On the sibling RAG project reasoning was ~89% of the bill; reading one short complaint is not a task that needs it. A 30s timeout and two retries, because a hung call holds the webhook open.

nodes.name: Decide if a human must see it
nodes.notes: needs_human is OUR rule, not the model's opinion: unsure, or no charger named, or critical. The model is never asked this question, because it is already being asked whether it is confident - and two fields encoding one state is how the sibling project spent a whole day on a bug.

nodes.name: Store what the model made of it

parameters.query:
insert into intake.classification
    (report_id, model, site, charger_label, symptom, severity, confident, needs_human, note)
values ($1, $2, nullif($3, ''), nullif($4, ''), $5, $6, $7, $8, nullif($9, ''))
returning id, needs_human

nodes.notes: A new row per attempt, never an update. nullif() turns the model's empty strings into real NULLs, because 'absent' and 'the empty string' answer different questions and only one of them survives a WHERE clause. This is also where a fifth severity is rejected by the database.

nodes.name: Reply to the reporter

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "report": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id, "classification": $json.id, "severity": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity, "charger": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label, "symptom": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom, "needs_human": $json.needs_human, "note": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.note } }}

nodes.notes: Every value is read from a NAMED node, not from $json. An item's shape changes at every node, and after an INSERT only the RETURNING columns survive - $json.report_id was undefined here and n8n dropped the key silently.

main.node: Store the report as it arrived
Decide if a human must see it
Store what the model made of it
